sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT (PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE A.Y. KOGJE) NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/676/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined 1.

The present appeal by the Insurance Company is preferred under Section 173 read with Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 against judgment and award passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi) and 3rd Additional District Judge, Ahmedabad (Rural) at Mirzapur dated 09-09-2016 in M.A.C.P. No.1954 of 2008.

entities.text: 3rd Additional District Judge, Ahmedabad (Rural) at Mirzapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Under the impugned judgment and award, compensation to tune of Rs.18,65,000/- have been awarded with direction of appropriating such compensation considering the claimants to be parents, widow and children of the deceased.
2. The Appeal came to be admitted by order dated 03-02-2017 in separate order in Civil Application for disbursement of the compensation.
3. From the record, it appears that Advocate notice in view of subsequent development was issued under order dated 16-06-2025 by Additional Registrar (Judicial).
However, none has appeared on behalf of the claimants.
4. The Court may refer to Cross Objection filed on behalf of the claimants, which was also admitted and ordered to be heard with First Appeal by order dated 02-11-2017.
This Court has passed order on 01-09- 2025 calling for Record and Proceedings from the Tribunal.
5. Considering the nature of dispute involved and assistance of learned Advocate representing the appellant-Insurance Company, the matter is taken up for final hearing.

6. Learned Advocate for the appellant-Insurance Company has submitted that an error is committed by the Tribunal in considering notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- in absence of any documentary or oral evidence regarding monthly income of the deceased.

C/FA/676/2017 JUDGMENT DAT Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd vs Konbiah Alias Konbiya Mathhu Alias ... on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199568750/
2

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the Tribunal has erred in considering prospective income of the deceased at the rate of 30%, as there was no evidence or proved regular income of the deceased at the time of accident.

It is also submitted that the claimant being self-employed, the Tribunal ought to have followed law laid down by the Apex court in case of Smt. Sarla Verma V. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 S.C.C. 121 to the extent that for the purpose of prospective income,
actual income is only to be considered at the time of death.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Verma V. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 S.C.C. 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. The Cross Objection filed by the claimants was on the ground that the deceased was owner of two trucks in the transport business and one truck was being driven by himself and therefore, his income ought to have been considered at Rs.20,000/- per month.

It is also pleaded that the Tribunal has erred in ignoring oral evidence of cleaner of the truck of the deceased at Exh-35 as well as evidence of Officer of Shri Ram Transport Finance at Exh-36, which would indicate that the deceased was paying installment to tune of Rs.8,324/- per month and also salary to the cleaner and therefore, income of Rs.10,000/- is far below the actual income, which ought to have been assessed.

8. Having considered the rival submissions of the parties and having perused the documents on record, the facts which are not much in dispute are with regard to manner and method, in which the accident took place i.e. on 03-08-2008 at 3.30 am, while the deceased was driving the truck bearing registration No.GJ-03-V-4818 between Ankleshwar to Morbi.

When the truck caught damaged and was required to be repaired on road and while doing so, the deceased was undertaking the repair work with necessary light signals and partitions, despite which erring NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/676/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined truck being driven in rash and negligent manner collided with stationary truck of the deceased, resulting into serious head injuries and succumbing to the injuries on the spot.
9. In this connection, FIR was registered with Borsad Police Station vide C.R. No.I-177 of 2008.

The deceased was aged 35 years and was survived by the parents, widow, son and daughter and age of the deceased was 35 years, the Claim was made to tune of Rs.75,00,000/- contending that income of the deceased was to tune of Rs.35,000/- per month out of driving of truck and agricultural income.

10. It appears that the Tribunal had treated offending vehicle to be solely negligent had granted compensation by applying parameters to income assessed to tune of Rs.10,000/- per month at the time of accident.

Thereby granting compensation as under:
 Compensation of Rs. Under the he

 50,000/- Towards Consortium  50,000/- Towards Loss of Love and affect  10,000/- Towards Transportation and Fune Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd vs Konbiah Alias Konbiya Mathhu Alias ... on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199568750/
3  18,65,000/- Total Compensation 11.

Considering the contention of the appellant-Insurance Company regarding notional income assessed at Rs.10,000/-, it would be pertinent to observe that evidence which has come on record, is to the effect that the deceased himself was owner of the truck and was paying salary to tune of Rs.6,000/- per month to the cleaner (Exh-35) and also, installment of Rs.8,324/- to Finance Company (Exh-36), Officer of Shri Ram Transport Finance.
 
 C/FA/676/2017 JUDGMENT DAT  
12.

In view of the aforesaid fact coming on record and contended by the claimants in their Cross Objection, the Court is of the view that monthly income of the deceased ought to have been treated at Rs.12,500/- per month instead of Rs.10,000/-.
Age of the deceased being 35 years, prospective income will be to tune of 40%, which comes to Rs.17,500/- per month (Rs.12,500/- + 5000).
It is apparent on the record that there were five dependents to the deceased and therefore,  amount is to be deducted, which comes to Rs.4,375/-.
Accordingly, loss of income suffered by the claimants would be to tune of Rs.13,125/- (13,125/- x 12 = 1,57,500/-) per annum.
The Tribunal has in its judgment and award applied multiplier of 15 in Para-20 of impugned judgment and award.

However, considering the age of the deceased being 35 years and applying principle as laid down by the Apex Court, age of the deceased being 35 years, multiplier of 16 will have to be applied and therefore, amount of compensation would be Rs.25,20,200/-.
13.
To bring just compensation in conformity with the decision of the Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited v/s. Pranay Sethi and Others.

In view of the aforesaid reasoning, the impugned judgment and award stands modified to aforesaid extent.
For the reasons recorded hereinabove, the following order is passed:
The present appeal is rejected and Cross Objection is allowed accordingly in above terms.

[B]. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount Rs.9,33,500/- at the rate of interest of 9% from the date of claim petition till its realisation before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and / or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon if any, to the claimant, by `Account Payee Cheque' / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.

[D]. While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the Courts fees, if not paid,
in accordance with the Rules.
[E]. Record & Proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.

C/FA/676/2017 JUDGMENT DAT  
16.
The Court fees to be calculated in accordance with the enhance compensation now granted.
The present appeal is rejected and Cross Objection is allowed accordingly in above terms.
